newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL up after S&P takes stake.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL up after S&P takes stake.

text.p: Shares of Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) jumped nearly 10 percent on Friday after Standard & Poor's said it will buy 9.6 percent equity in the firm, brokers said.
The share was up 26.75 rupees, or 9.91 percent, to 296.75 on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
CRISIL said on Friday the global rating agency signed a share purchase agreement subject to approval by the Reserve Bank of India.
"These shares are currently held by the Asian Development Bank, which invested in CRISIL in 1988 to play a catalytic role in its establishment," the statement said.
S&P's and CRISIL formed a strategic business alliance last year for analytical and business development cooperation.

"We are delighted to strengthen our ties with CRISIL, which continues to build its analytical capabilities and credibility in India and throughout the region," the statement quoted Leo C. O'Neill, S&P's president and chief rating officer, as saying.
The share has gained 32 percent since April 28 when it closed at 224.91 on the BSE.
